choice.description: Under screening rule SR-3, how should this claim be classified?

contexts:
RIVERBEND LEGAL AID CLINIC — INTAKE SCREENING NOTE

Screening rule SR-3 (limitation, property-damage claims against contractors):
  A claim is time-barred if it is filed more than 3 years after the date on which the claimant knew, or reasonably should have known, of the damage. No other tolling rule applies to this claim type in this jurisdiction. If the knowledge date cannot be pinned down, use the LATEST date consistent with the claimant's own account (most favourable to the claimant). Screeners mark a case "insufficient_information" only if even that latest possible date cannot be bounded.

Intake interview, 2026-09-16 (screener: T. Alvarez)
  Client: Noor Haddad. Opponent: DryWell Roofing LLC (roof replacement completed 2022-11-08).
  Q: When did you first notice the water damage?
  A: "Honestly I don't remember the exact day. It was after Easter 2023 — we'd had guests over for Easter and the ceiling was fine then. And I know it was before my birthday, May 29th, because my sister saw the stain when she came for my birthday dinner and told me I had to call someone... which I only did in the autumn."
  Q: Any documents?
  A: "The first quote from another roofer is from October 2023."
  Planned filing date if we take the case: 2026-09-25.
Screener remark: "Exact knowledge date unknown — client can't recall. Flag as insufficient info?"
